pairs_touching.what_says_this: Two POSSIBLY-RELATION groups (G0491, G0530). B's own notation (b_notations) defines a Yoga operator family Y:(K_t,O,C,G)->K_{t+1} with named members 'Y_B, Y_D'; the group note gives the correspondence 'Buddhi=discrimination function' and explicitly names 'Yoga-1 (Discrimination, Y_B=B(K,x))' as one of three named simulations. A's notation is exactly this specific transition 'K_t -> Buddhi -> qualified transition -> K_{t+1}'. B generalizes A's single Buddhi-discrimination transition into one member (Y_B) of a broader family of Yoga operators (Y_B, Y_D, plus Yoga-2/Yoga-3).
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If Y_B was independently defined without reference to the specific hpa-buddhi-discrimination-second-pass document (i.e. both independently derive a discrimination operator from the same Gita/Yoga source material rather than one building on the other), EXTENSION would overstate direct dependency; group note G0530 does say the Yoga framework was 'first proposed in B0054 and reused/restated in B0055', suggesting some continuity of authorship/session but not an explicit citation of A by name.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Yoga \neq Knowledge ... K_1=K_2 but Y(K_1)\neq Y(K_2)
rationale_evidence.statement: Yoga must not be identified with Knowledge or 'more knowledge'; it is a relationship/transformation of epistemic state. Two systems can hold K_1=K_2 while Y(K_1) != Y(K_2), because context, purpose, observations, uncertainty, or operational state differs -- connecting to the Step 287 distinction between structural, semantic and observational equality. Also proposes making Yoga explicitly temporal: K_{t+1}=Y_t(K_t,O_t,C_t), noting dK/dt may not be meaningful as a continuous derivative since KnowledgeOS state may be discrete/event-driven, so K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t) is preferred, with Yoga as a family of possible transition strategies over delta.

## Rationale
Yoga must not be identified with Knowledge or 'more knowledge'; it is a relationship/transformation of epistemic state. Two systems can hold K_1=K_2 while Y(K_1) != Y(K_2), because context, purpose, observations, uncertainty, or operational state differs -- connecting to the Step 287 distinction between structural, semantic and observational equality. Also proposes making Yoga explicitly temporal: K_{t+1}=Y_t(K_t,O_t,C_t), noting dK/dt may not be meaningful as a continuous derivative since KnowledgeOS state may be discrete/event-driven, so K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o_t) is preferred, with Yoga as a family of possible transition strategies over delta. [S2225]
